Hi Alice / Tom —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- Goals you called out:
  • Latency SLO: p95 target in the ~150-200ms range for typical requests (details below)
  • Concurrency/throughput: target ~50 concurrent users with spikes up to 250 req/s
  • Streaming: partial-token streaming required for chat UI to reduce perceived latency
  • Context window: occasional long histories up to ~32k tokens; average session ~6k tokens

- Open items for us to validate (can you confirm the items in bold?):
  1) Typical output length: ~512 tokens (50th-90th percentile), with worst-case up to 2k tokens
  2) Payload sizes: average input ~6k tokens, sometimes full 32k context with long histories
  3) Peak concurrency / burst behavior: are bursts predictable (cron/batch) or user-driven?
  4) Security/compliance constraints: any restrictions on sending customer data to hosted environments?

Could you share a small sample payload set (anonymized) and confirm the output token distribution? I attached a short meeting_notes.txt and would appreciate sample_payload.json if you have it.

Next steps we propose from Redwood:
  - Internal perf check with rishi/vivek to validate feasibility and rough estimates
  - Short pilot (1-2 weeks) on Dedicated capacity to measure real p95/p99 under your workload
  - Follow-up call to review pilot results and sizing

Thanks — I’ll loop our infra team in and share a first-pass estimate by tomorrow.

Thanks for the clear recap — confirming key numbers from our side: 

- Latency targets: p95 <= 150ms is our ideal target for interactive flows. We can accept p95 up to 200ms for edge cases, but p99 should remain under 600ms ideally.
- Typical output size: 512 tokens median, 95th percentile ~1k tokens, max 2k tokens for some report generations.
- Context window: average session history ~6k tokens; roughly 10% of requests include the full 32k token history when the user pulls long transcripts.
- Concurrency/throughput: 50 steady concurrent users per region, peak bursts up to 250 req/s (user-driven bursts during end-of-day reporting).
- Streaming requirement: yes — UI expects token-by-token or small-chunk streaming to start rendering the assistant response within ~50-80ms of generation start.

We've attached a small anonymized sample_payload.json and two example transcripts. Security: we can start with your hosted environment under standard DPA; will escalate if needed.

Marissa —

Quick feasibility notes after a first pass on the sample payload and workload profile: 

1) Context window impact:
   - For decoder-only models, attention computation and KV cache lookups grow with sequence length. Average 6k context is manageable; the occasional 32k window is the costly case.
   - On A100-class hardware with our optimized kernels and prefix caching, we estimate p95 ~140ms for a 512-token output with 6k context (single-request, no coalesced batching).
   - For a full 32k context, p95 could increase to ~280-350ms unless we apply specific mitigations (see below).

2) Streaming behaviors:
   - Streaming helps perceived latency by sending the first token(s) early. However, the time to compute the first partial tokens still depends on the initial decoder steps and applying the context. If the model is configured to emit at smaller chunk sizes (e.g., 16-32 tokens), the UI can render sooner (50-100ms), but the overall end-to-end time to finish a 512-token output remains similar.

3) Concurrency and batching:
   - Host/shared capacity can hit higher 99th-percentile tails during bursts. For predictable p95 under concurrent bursts, Dedicated capacity with reserved lanes is recommended.
   - For your targets (50 steady concurrents, burst to 250 req/s), we recommend a Dedicated pool with autoscale thresholds + 4 concurrency lanes and an initial commit sized for 250 rps bursts.

4) Mitigations & recommendations:
   - Use a model variant optimized for long-context (sparse attention or chunked attention) for the 32k path.
   - Enable prefix/KV caching for session history to avoid re-attending the entire context each request.
   - Apply 8-bit quantization + optimized kernels to reduce per-token compute; expect 15-25% latency improvement.
   - Tune batching parameters: max_batch_latency to 15-25ms and a conservative max_batch_size to avoid tail amplification on p95.

5) Expected pilot configuration:
   - 2-week Dedicated trial: 4x A100-equivalent instances, prefix cache enabled, quantized model variant.
   - We'll capture p50/p95/p99, streaming-first-byte times, and end-to-end completion time for 512/1k/2k outputs.

I attached a short perf_estimate_v1.csv with approximate numbers for the configurations above. Also see our runbook for context-window latency tradeoffs: https://redwood.ai/runbooks/context-window-latency

If this looks good I can draft a slightly more conservative SLO estimate to share with FinCo (include safety margin for their 32k requests).

Thanks,
Rishi

Hi Alice / Tom —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for the sample payload. Rishi did a great first pass and attached an initial perf estimate. Key takeaways for you: 

- For your typical 6k context + 512-token outputs, p95 in the 140-160ms range is realistic with our suggested Dedicated pilot configuration.
- The 32k context path will materially increase p95 (roughly 280-350ms in our estimate) unless we adopt long-context model variants + prefix caching.
- Streaming will improve perceived latency (first bytes in ~50-100ms) but doesn't eliminate the additional compute cost for long contexts.

Proposed next steps:
  1) Run a 2-week Dedicated pilot with the config Rishi outlined (we'll size for your 250 rps bursts).
  2) Capture the metric set listed in the attached SOW placeholder and share a short results review call — can you pick a slot here: https://cal.com/marissa/30min ?
  3) If pilot numbers look good, we can present a formal SLO and Dedicated sizing recommendation and an optional roadmap to the 32k-optimized model variant.

I can send a short SOW for the pilot and a DocuSign if you want to accelerate.

Would you like us to schedule the pilot kickoff next week?
